title: Six Teams, Ten Matches, Four Spots: Inside IPL 2026's Thrilling Playoff Race
excerpt: After KKR's record-setting demolition of GT and Marsh's masterclass sinking CSK, the IPL 2026 standings are wide open with the league stage entering its final weekend
body:
With ten matches left in the league stage and six teams still mathematically alive, the IPL 2026 playoff race has entered its most volatile phase. Friday's double-header — Lucknow Super Giants dismantling Chennai Super Kings, followed by Kolkata Knight Riders stunning Gujarat Titans at Eden Gardens — reshuffled the standings and injected fresh chaos into what had seemed a straightforward qualification picture.

## The Top Two: RCB and GT Hold Firm

Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Gujarat Titans sit level on 16 points with identical 8-4 records, separated only by net run rate. RCB's NRR of +1.053, the best in the tournament, gives them the edge for the all-important first-place finish — and the safety net of Qualifier 1 rather than the Eliminator.

But GT's 29-run defeat to KKR at Eden Gardens has introduced a wrinkle. Kolkata's 247/2 — powered by Finn Allen's extraordinary 93 off just 35 balls and Angkrish Raghuvanshi's 82 off 44 — was the highest total ever posted against the Titans in IPL history. Even Shubman Gill's counter-attacking 85 couldn't bridge the gap.

## The Middle Scramble: SRH, PBKS, RR, CSK

The real drama lies between third and sixth. Sunrisers Hyderabad (14 points, 7 wins) currently hold the third qualifying spot but have no margin for error. Punjab Kings sit fourth on 13 points with a positive NRR, while Rajasthan Royals and Chennai Super Kings are locked on 12 points apiece with two matches remaining each.

CSK's playoff prospects took a devastating blow when Mitchell Marsh's 90 off 38 balls — including four sixes in a single over — propelled LSG to a seven-wicket demolition. The loss dropped Chennai's NRR and left them needing results elsewhere to go their way. MS Dhoni's presence in the squad had generated enormous buzz, but his side now faces a near-impossible mathematical path.

## KKR's Last Stand, DC's Long Shot

KKR's emphatic victory over GT was as much about survival as it was about spectacle. Sunil Narine, playing his 200th IPL match for a single franchise — a record in itself — took 2/29 to complement the batting fireworks. But with 10 points from 12 games, KKR likely need to win their remaining two matches by massive margins to overturn their NRR deficit.

Delhi Capitals, also on 10 points, face similarly steep odds. Mumbai Indians and Lucknow Super Giants have already been eliminated.

## The Diaspora Is Watching

The IPL's reach has never been wider. The 2026 season has crossed 1.1 billion cumulative viewers, with JioStar's digital platform driving a massive surge in Connected TV viewership. For the estimated 32 million NRIs worldwide, the playoff race is appointment viewing — even when it means 6 AM alarms in Toronto or midnight streams in London.

Saturday's double-header — Punjab Kings hosting RCB in Mohali and Delhi Capitals facing Rajasthan Royals at the Arun Jaitley Stadium — could settle two qualification questions in a single evening. For every franchise between 10 and 14 points, the mathematics is unforgiving: win everything, and hope.

The playoffs are set for Ahmedabad, with Qualifier 1 on May 26, the Eliminator on May 27, Qualifier 2 on May 29, and the final on May 31.
